messages:
maria: Heads-up — regtest perf alert after merging PR #6199. Microbench for kv_cache_lookup shows ~3.2% regression and batch scheduler wait p95 jumped from 9ms -> 21ms. Failing threshold is the PR gate (regtests/perf/unit/kv_cache_lookup:diff > 2%).

maria: paste of the failing lines:
```
KV cache microbench: baseline=0.512ms/op, head=0.528ms/op, diff=+3.125% (threshold 2.0%)
Batch scheduler p95: baseline=9.1ms, head=21.4ms
--probe: kernel_selector path: selected=fast_matmul_v2 rather than fast_matmul_v1
```

ci-bot: perf-regression-checker: PR 6199 exceeded perf threshold on 2 tests. See https://ci.internal/redwood/6199/jobs/42 for details.

andrew: ugh. 6199 touched the batching heuristics and kernel selector fallback order, right? i commented about kernel heuristics on the PR.

maria: yup — PR changed "prefer_small_batch_kernels" ordering and added a fast_matmul_v2 path intended for long sequences. The microbench uses short sequences (32) so selector should've picked v1. Something upstream probability in the selector changed.

sam: I can grab a local repro. running regtest locally now. if it's a simple ordering bug we can revert ordering or add a guard for short seqs. will report back in ~15m. :coffee:

leo: tagging @andrew — if selector heuristics are non-deterministic across runs maybe we need to pin kernel choice for microbench to avoid flaky perf tests. CI shouldn't fail on heuristics randomness.

andrew: agree. also want to rule out KV cache interaction — PR added a tiny change to prefix caching logic (not supposed to affect lookup hot path) but could change cache alignment and indirectly affect scheduler batching. odd.

sam: local regtest reproduces reliably on my laptop. looks like the selector picks v2 for seq_len=32 about 60% of runs. i ran 20 iterations: 12 picks v2, 8 picks v1.

maria: so it's non-deterministic. that explains why CI started failing after merging since it flipped a threshold. we should either fix selector determinism or make perf-test robust.

leo: quick mitigation: update the perf/unit test to assert against the best-of-3 median rather than single-run threshold. longer term: root-cause selector randomness.

andrew: can we bisect to the specific commit in the PR that introduced the nondeterminism? i'll run git bisect against the branch. will report commit id.

ci-bot: deploy-bot: started a canary rollback for PR 6199 on dedicated staging to stop noisy regressions.

sam: bisect found the change — commit 3d9a8f7 modified the kernel scoring tie-breaker to prefer kernels with lower expected memory, but it used a float RNG seed from thread-local scheduling which isn't stable across runs. changing to deterministic tie-breaker fixes the selection. patch below:
```diff
- score += randf() * 1e-6
+ score += (kernel_id % 7) * 1e-6  # deterministic tie-break
```

maria: nice find. do we want to revert the PR or push a fix in a follow-up? this is a rollback blocker for the release.

andrew: push fix asap and run regtests. if fix lands today we can un-revert and re-run the rollout. otherwise revert to unblock release.

sam: opened PR 6202 with the deterministic tie-breaker and explicit comment about why randomness is unacceptable in selector. linked to 6199. https://git.internal/redwood/6199 -> 6202

ci-bot: perf-regression-checker: running regtests against PR 6202...

ci-bot: perf-regression-checker: PR 6202 passed; diffs below:
```
KV cache microbench: baseline=0.512ms/op, head=0.513ms/op, diff=+0.2% (threshold 2.0%)
Batch scheduler p95: baseline=9.1ms, head=9.3ms
```

maria: rolling forward with 6202. thanks @sam for the bisect and fix. leaving notes for postmortem: avoid seeded/thread-local randomness in kernel selection, add deterministic tie-breaker tests, and relax perf test to median-of-3 until selector determinism is guaranteed.

andrew: also adding a small unit test to assert kernel selection is stable for fixed env and seed. will open follow-up.

leo: logging the incident to perf-regressions channel with action items. :memo:

maria: resolved — marking this thread closed. :white_check_mark:
